summary: The bin component holds selfware's auxiliary binaries — offline tools that ground and evaluate the loop rather than run inside it. codegraph builds a JSON dependency graph (CodeGraph of nodes and edges: functions, structs, enums, traits, modules; 'uses'/'implements'/'contains' edges, plus fusion_groups for cyclic clusters) that gives the planner structural grounding. vlm_gen_fixtures generates PNG benchmark fixtures across six escalating difficulty levels (TUI state, diagnostics, architecture, profiling, layout, evolution), and vlm_bench_run (VlmBenchRunner over VlmBenchConfig) drives a vision-language model against them and emits JSON/Markdown reports. On the loop these are 'foundation' (codegraph as structural substrate) and 'eval' (the VLM harness measuring the loop's multimodal perception offline).
context_basis: Recommendations were formed by reading src/bin/ (codegraph.rs, vlm_bench_run.rs, vlm_gen_fixtures.rs) in the context of the full engine's ~600k-token budget framing, so each move treats these binaries as offline substrate and eval harnesses that inform the loop without competing for its live turn budget.

examples.title: Build a code graph to ground planning
examples.intent: Produce a whole-repo structural map the planner can navigate before touching code.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: codegraph regex-scans the crate and emits codegraph.json with nodes (id,label,kind,path,lines,tokens_estimate,complexity) and edges; the loop plans against this map instead of blind file walks, saving perceive budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread over the repo root node to unfold the full CodeGraph as a spatial constellation of module and type nodes.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes bloom by kind color (fn/struct/enum/trait/module) with edges drawn as 'uses'/'implements'/'contains' strands.

examples.mini_scenario: Before a refactor, cargo run --bin codegraph writes codegraph.json and the planner loads it to see which modules touch the target type.
examples.pitfall: codegraph is deprecated (2026-07-26) and emits duplicate node ids and dangling edges — prefer selfware self-evolve's graph; use this only as a reference fallback.

examples.title: Estimate per-node token cost for budgeting
examples.intent: Attach a token estimate to each code node so the loop can size reads before it makes them.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each CodeGraph node carries tokens_estimate and a low/medium/high complexity tag; the planner uses these to pick which nodes fit the remaining budget, shaping how much of the codebase a single iteration ingests.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch a node to reveal its token-estimate meter and complexity tier.
touch_interaction.visual: A cost pill shows the token estimate; complexity renders as a three-step green/amber/red gauge.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop has 40k budget left; it picks three low-complexity nodes under 12k tokens total rather than one high-complexity module.
examples.pitfall: tokens_estimate is a heuristic from line counts, not a real tokenizer count — treat it as a rough envelope, not a hard budget guarantee.

examples.title: Surface context actions per node
examples.intent: Offer the loop a menu of what it can do with each code node and the cost of each.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each node lists context_actions (inspect, read_full, read_skeleton, alter, build_new) with token/time estimates; the loop selects an affordance sized to its budget instead of always reading full.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press a node to open its context-actions wheel of inspect/read_full/read_skeleton/alter/build_new.
touch_interaction.visual: A radial menu fans out, each spoke labeled with its token and time estimate.

examples.mini_scenario: Rather than read_full a 900-line module, the loop picks read_skeleton to get its shape for a fraction of the tokens.
examples.pitfall: Don't default to read_full for every node — the skeleton affordance exists precisely to keep the perceive step within budget.

examples.title: Detect cyclic clusters with fusion groups
examples.intent: Warn the planner about circular dependencies before it edits into a knot.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: codegraph computes fusion_groups (binary mutual deps, trinary cycles, quaternary diamonds); the loop reasons that these clusters must change together, so it plans them as a unit rather than one file at a time.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate a fusion group to view the cycle from different angles and see which edges close the loop.
touch_interaction.visual: Cyclic edges glow in a closed ring; binary/trinary/quaternary groups are tinted by their fusion pattern.

examples.mini_scenario: codegraph flags a binary fusion between config and loader; the loop plans a joint edit instead of breaking one and stranding the other.
examples.pitfall: Ignoring fusion_groups leads to half-applied edits that leave a cycle inconsistent — treat a group as an atomic unit of change.

examples.title: Run the code graph as an offline foundation step
examples.intent: Keep graph construction out of the live turn budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: codegraph runs as a standalone binary (cargo run --bin codegraph) from the project root and writes a file; the loop consumes the artifact later, so heavy scanning never competes with in-turn reasoning.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick the codegraph node into the offline tray to schedule a background regeneration.
touch_interaction.visual: The node moves to a separate offline lane and shows a build spinner detached from the live loop.

examples.mini_scenario: Overnight, codegraph regenerates the artifact; the next morning's loop loads a fresh map with zero in-turn cost.
examples.pitfall: A stale codegraph.json misleads the planner — regenerate after large refactors, since the file is a snapshot not a live view.

examples.title: Generate benchmark fixtures for VLM eval
examples.intent: Produce the visual stimuli the eval harness will grade the loop's perception against.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: vlm_gen_fixtures renders 18 PNGs across six levels via text_to_png into level subdirs (ensure_fixture_dir); these become the fixed ground truth that lets eval measure multimodal perception reproducibly.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread over the fixtures node to lay out all six level folders and their rendered PNGs.
touch_interaction.visual: Thumbnails tile by level (l1..mega), each folder chip badged with its PNG count.

examples.mini_scenario: cargo run --features vlm-bench --bin vlm_gen_fixtures writes l1_tui_state through mega_evolution so the harness has stable inputs.
examples.pitfall: Regenerating fixtures mid-benchmark invalidates comparability — freeze the fixture set before a scoring run.

examples.title: Ladder difficulty from TUI state to evolution
examples.intent: Structure eval so perception is tested across escalating visual complexity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The Difficulty enum (Easy..Mega) maps to level folders (l1 TUI state, l2 diagnostics, l3 architecture, l4 profiling, l5 layout, mega evolution); eval walks the ladder to find where the loop's vision breaks down.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag along the difficulty rail to preview each level's fixtures in ascending complexity.
touch_interaction.visual: A rail of six stops lights up sequentially; harder stops carry a denser, warmer tint.

examples.mini_scenario: Eval runs Easy through Hard cleanly but drops accuracy at l4 profiling flamegraphs, pinpointing the loop's perception limit.
examples.pitfall: Skipping intermediate levels hides where degradation begins — run the ladder in order, not just the extremes.

examples.title: Configure the benchmark runner
examples.intent: Pin the endpoint, model, and sampling so eval results are reproducible.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VlmBenchConfig captures endpoint, model, concurrency, max_tokens, temperature, timeout, and dirs; fixing these makes a benchmark run a controlled measurement of the loop's perception rather than a moving target.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the runner node to open its config wheel of endpoint/model/temperature/concurrency.
touch_interaction.visual: Each parameter renders as an adjustable dial; changed-from-default dials glow to flag non-standard runs.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator sets --model qwen/qwen3.5-9b --temperature 0.2 so two runs on the same fixtures are directly comparable.
examples.pitfall: Changing temperature or model between runs invalidates comparison — record the VlmBenchConfig alongside every report.

examples.title: Drive the VLM against fixtures
examples.intent: Actually score the model's visual reasoning on the frozen fixture set.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VlmBenchRunner sends each fixture to the OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint and collects per-level results; this is the eval act that verifies whether the loop's perception layer meets bar before it's trusted in production.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the run node to launch the benchmark; a progress edge sweeps through each fixture.
touch_interaction.visual: A fill bar advances per level; passing fixtures mark green, failures red as they resolve.

examples.mini_scenario: The runner sends dashboard_error.png and grades whether the VLM correctly reports the connection-error state.
examples.pitfall: A flaky endpoint inflates failures — respect the timeout and concurrency settings so contention doesn't masquerade as poor perception.

examples.title: Emit dual JSON and Markdown reports
examples.intent: Produce both a machine-readable and a human-readable record of eval outcomes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The runner writes vlm_benchmark_report.json and .md into vlm_results/; the JSON feeds automated tracking while the Markdown lets a human diagnose, closing the learn loop over perception quality.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the report node to flip between its JSON and Markdown faces.
touch_interaction.visual: The card flips like a coin: one side structured JSON, the other rendered Markdown with a summary table.

examples.mini_scenario: After a run, the Markdown report shows l5 layout at 60% while the JSON feeds a dashboard tracking the trend over releases.
examples.pitfall: Consuming only the JSON loses the human narrative; reading only the Markdown loses machine tracking — keep both in the loop's memory.

examples.title: Test diagnostic-reading with l2 fixtures
examples.intent: Check specifically whether the loop can read compiler errors from a screenshot.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: l2_diagnostics fixtures (lifetime_error, type_mismatch, trait_bound) probe the exact perception the loop needs when a build screenshot is its only evidence; eval here validates a load-bearing capability.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the l2 level chip to run only the diagnostics fixtures.
touch_interaction.visual: Three fixture thumbnails light up; each shows the parsed-vs-expected error side by side.

examples.mini_scenario: The harness feeds trait_bound.png and checks the VLM identifies the missing Send bound the loop would need to fix.
examples.pitfall: Diagnostic fixtures are text-heavy — a low render resolution can fail the model for legibility, not reasoning; keep text_to_png crisp.

examples.title: Test architecture comprehension with l3 fixtures
examples.intent: Validate the loop can read system diagrams into a mental model.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: l3_architecture fixtures (evolution_diagram, agent_pipeline, safety_layers) test whether the VLM extracts component flow; eval confirms the loop can perceive its own architecture diagrams as structured knowledge.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread on the agent_pipeline fixture to compare the diagram against the model's extracted stage list.
touch_interaction.visual: Detected stages (Parser, Context, Planner, Executor) highlight on the diagram as the model names them.

examples.mini_scenario: Eval shows the VLM correctly reads the four-stage agent pipeline, so the loop can trust it to interpret diagrams.
examples.pitfall: Diagram fixtures encode a specific layout — don't over-fit eval to these exact PNGs, or the score won't generalize to novel diagrams.

examples.title: Test profiling readouts with l4 fixtures
examples.intent: Check the loop can read flamegraphs and memory profiles from images.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: l4_profiling fixtures (simple_flamegraph, multithread_profile, memory_profile) test perception of performance visuals; eval validates whether the loop can act on profiling evidence delivered as a screenshot.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the flamegraph fixture to see which frame the model named as hottest.
touch_interaction.visual: The identified hot frame (e.g. hnsw::search_layer) highlights in the flamegraph with a heat overlay.

examples.mini_scenario: Eval feeds simple_flamegraph.png and checks the VLM names search_layer as the hotspot the loop would target.
examples.pitfall: Flamegraph reading is a hard level — a failure here bounds where the loop can rely on visual profiling, so record it, don't discard it.

examples.title: Test layout reasoning with l5 fixtures
examples.intent: Validate the loop can parse nested TUI layouts from an image.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: l5_layout fixtures (simple_split, dashboard_grid, complex_nested) test spatial decomposition; eval measures whether the loop can perceive a UI's structure well enough to act on the right panel.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the complex_nested fixture to drill into how deep the model resolved the layout tree.
touch_interaction.visual: Nested regions outline progressively as the model reports each nesting level, up to depth four.

examples.mini_scenario: Eval checks the VLM identifies the 3x2 dashboard_grid regions so a downstream loop could target the status pane.
examples.pitfall: Deeply nested layouts stress the model; a miss at depth four bounds the loop's reliable UI-parsing depth.

examples.title: Track UI evolution with mega fixtures
examples.intent: Measure whether the loop can perceive change across successive UI iterations.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: mega_evolution fixtures (iteration_01, progression_pair, iteration_03) test before/after comprehension; eval validates the loop's ability to perceive its own evolution, feeding the learn stage of self-improvement.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw a connection between iteration_01 and iteration_03 to have the model narrate what changed.
touch_interaction.visual: A diff edge links the two thumbnails; added panels highlight green, removed ones red.

examples.mini_scenario: Eval feeds progression_pair and checks the VLM describes the v0.1 to v0.3 jump the loop's evolution engine produced.
examples.pitfall: Progression fixtures encode one specific evolution story — don't treat mastery here as general change-detection across arbitrary UIs.

examples.title: Gate the harness behind a feature flag
examples.intent: Keep the VLM eval tooling out of default builds.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Both VLM binaries require --features vlm-bench; this keeps heavy eval dependencies off the loop's default build path so production stays lean, and eval is opt-in.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the vlm-bench feature toggle to enable or disable the eval binaries on the canvas.
touch_interaction.visual: The VLM nodes render greyed and non-interactive until the vlm-bench flag is toggled on.

examples.mini_scenario: A production build omits vlm-bench so the eval harness never ships; a CI eval job enables the flag to run it.
examples.pitfall: Don't wire eval into the default build — the fixtures and VLM client are eval-only and would bloat the loop's runtime footprint.

examples.title: Tune concurrency against endpoint capacity
examples.intent: Match benchmark parallelism to what the model endpoint can serve.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VlmBenchConfig.concurrency controls how many fixtures run in parallel; setting it to the endpoint's real capacity keeps eval fast without contention corrupting the measurement.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drag the concurrency slider on the runner node to set parallel request count.
touch_interaction.visual: Parallel request lanes appear beneath the node, one per unit of concurrency, throttling when overloaded.

examples.mini_scenario: A local LM Studio serves one request at a time; concurrency stays at 1 so latency reflects the model, not queueing.
examples.pitfall: Over-high concurrency against a single-slot endpoint inflates timeouts and skews the eval — size it to real capacity.

examples.title: Render text to PNG deterministically
examples.intent: Produce identical fixtures every generation so eval is repeatable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: text_to_png renders each character at a fixed 8x16 cell, so re-running vlm_gen_fixtures yields byte-stable PNGs; eval can trust that a score change reflects the model, not fixture drift.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a fixture thumbnail to inspect its fixed 8x16 character grid.
touch_interaction.visual: A pixel grid overlays the rendered text, confirming each glyph occupies an exact cell.

examples.mini_scenario: Regenerating help_panel.png yields an identical file, so a diff against a prior run detects only real changes.
examples.pitfall: Any nondeterminism in rendering (fonts, timestamps) breaks reproducibility — keep the renderer pinned and free of variable content.

examples.title: Feed the code graph into evolution planning
examples.intent: Let structural knowledge shape which modules the loop chooses to evolve.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The CodeGraph's complexity tags and fusion_groups inform which nodes are safe to alter vs build_new; the loop's reasoning prioritizes low-complexity, low-coupling targets first.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw from the graph node to the plan node to seed evolution targets ranked by complexity.
touch_interaction.visual: The plan node fills with target rows sorted low-to-high complexity, coupled nodes grouped by fusion tint.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop picks an isolated low-complexity module to evolve first, deferring a high-complexity fusion cluster.
examples.pitfall: codegraph's known schema mismatch with consumers can misrank nodes — validate against the live evolve graph before committing a plan order.

examples.title: Separate eval artifacts from source
examples.intent: Keep generated fixtures and reports out of the source tree.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: vlm_gen_fixtures writes to vlm_fixtures/ and the runner to vlm_results/; isolating eval artifacts keeps the loop's codebase clean and the CodeGraph free of non-source noise.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick generated artifacts into the isolated artifact tray, away from the source constellation.
touch_interaction.visual: Fixture and report nodes drift into a bordered off-canvas tray tinted distinctly from source nodes.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator points --output_dir at vlm_results/ so reports never land in src/ where codegraph would scan them.
examples.pitfall: Letting eval artifacts leak into the source tree pollutes the CodeGraph with non-code nodes and inflates its token estimates.
